soundness_flags.label: ass:balanced-cell-masses
soundness_flags.one_line: The condition is labeled a standard Zeng et al. condition, but that cited paper explicitly allows arbitrary—including zero—cell masses and does not support the asserted balanced growing-multinomial assumption.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 5, Eq. (3), lines 278–293; p. 9, Theorem 2, lines 635–655; p. 20, lines 1620–1629
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper's model permits 0≤p_k≤1, its Theorem 2 gives the d/(n log n) squared-risk lower scale, and its 401(k) bootstrap/Gaussian intervals are explicitly described as potentially non-nominal.
The paper studies ATE inference under smoothness/shape restrictions and obtains finite-sample optimal procedures with normal known-variance errors; feasible unknown-error versions are asymptotic.

Assumption 5.1 imposes overlap, moments, a nondegenerate score scale, and nuisance product rates; Theorem 5.1 gives uniform asymptotic normality, variance replacement, and asymptotically valid ATE intervals.

source_verification_receipts.version: Annales de l'I.H.P. Probabilités et Statistiques 48(4), 2012
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Catoni studies i.i.d. real observations under global variance and kurtosis models and constructs bounded-influence mean procedures; it is a calibration template rather than a theorem for selected factorial statistics.
The paper establishes Cramér-type moderate deviations for self-normalized processes, including Studentized U-statistics under fixed-order conditions.
The paper gives selective confidence intervals for probabilities of unobserved multinomial events, including dimension-free bounds, rather than causal marked aggregates.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the Zeng citation on balanced-cell masses with a source that actually assumes a minimum cell-mass condition, or retag the condition as a novel local regularity assumption and justify why it is an intentionally restricted regular submodel.

State the heavy-cell truncation threshold, perturbation-block scheme, and score functional as explicit primitives before proving the global theorem; retain the open-ended question only for the constants and proof certificate.

Add a worked finite small-table example that computes the rare-cell score radius and its outward-rounded endpoints, making the constructive inference claim auditable independently of the asymptotic frontier.

recommended_next_step: Repair the unsupported standard-assumption citation/tag, then advance the revised honest-inference frontier to Stage 0.
